title: Clinical outcomes after implantation of a combination of intrastromal corneal ring segments in different optical zones in advanced keratoconus

license.statement: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 License)

groups.description: 32 eyes of 30 patients with advanced keratoconus (Kmax above 60 D, ABCD stage 4) treated with a 320-degree Ferrara ring segment in the 5-mm zone combined with a high-myopia ring segment in the 6-mm zone (femtosecond tunnels, one or two surgical stages); prior cross-linking excluded (Methods)

series.notes: mean ± SD; per-visit n printed in the cells (32 preoperative, 27 at 1 month, 31 at 3 months); Scheimpflug tomography (Pentacam, Methods)

exclusions.reason: latest follow-up after 6 months (range 6-24 months), no single dated time
figure only; the table cells are cited

notes: Context icrs: two ring segments (standard and high-myopia), no cross-linking during follow-up.
Rings were implanted in one or two surgical stages; the article does not say for two-stage eyes whether postoperative times count from the first or the second implantation.

Inclusion required a minimum follow-up of 6 months (eyes with less than 90 days excluded); kept because the analysis set is not restricted to eyes with every tabulated visit (27 and 31 eyes at 1 and 3 months) and the last tabulated visit is the late visit after 6 months.
Age group unstated: mean age ± SD only, consent from participants or legal guardians (Methods, Results).
BCVA, MRSE, mean K, K1, K2, tomographic astigmatism and asphericity (Table 1) are tabulated and not used.
